processing: Typical of raw pu-erh from Menghai: sun-dried green leaf (maocha), sold loose or pressed, with no ripe-style piling.
harvest_season: Spring is the prized picking, and spring leaf here is especially bitter and astringent at first, with a lingering sweet finish.
appearance_dry: Thick, plump, tightly rolled dark leaves.
appearance_wet: Thick, fleshy large leaves in olive green, as is typical of Bulang old-tree tea.
taste_profile: Strongly bitter in the first steeps, turning sweet after roughly five to seven infusions, with a long sweet finish; it holds up well over many steeps.

brewing.notes: Use less leaf than usual and very quick early steeps. The bitterness is the point, but if you overbrew it you never reach the sweetness that comes later.

vintage_note: Sold by harvest year, usually spring leaf pressed the same year, then drunk young or stored. Tree age makes a big price difference, so a cheap Lao Man'e is likely younger leaf.
description:
Lao Man'e is a Blang village in the northeast of the Bulang Mountains in Menghai County, at about 1,650 metres, and its tea is the benchmark of bitterness in raw pu-erh. People drink it for that, not in spite of it.

Both bitter and sweet tea types grow here, in old gardens with trees tall enough that pickers use bamboo ladders. The leaf follows the usual raw pu-erh route, ending up thick, plump and tightly rolled.

The first steeps are properly bitter, and the turn comes after about five to seven infusions, when it goes sweet and stays that way. Brew with less leaf and very short steeps, and do not give up after the second cup.

Check which type and which tree age you are buying. Bulang villages differ more than the reputation for bitterness suggests, and a label saying Bulang tells you much less than one naming the village.
history: The age of the village is told very differently: figures of over a thousand years and over 1,400 years both circulate, and neither is firmly documented. Claims of 500 to more than 1,000 years for the oldest trees belong to the same kind of estimate.
